commit_message:
urlapi: consume trailing dots after IPv4 numerical addresses

If the hostname is specified as an IPv4 numerical address and it is
followed by a single dot, acccept that as a valid IPv4 and remove the
dot when normalizing.

This prevents otherwise legitimate IPv4 hostnames to have trailing dots.
Seems to match what browsers do.

Extended test 1560 to verify.

Closes #21635

--- a/lib/urlapi.c
+++ b/lib/urlapi.c
@@ -494,10 +494,13 @@ static CURLUcode hostname_check(struct Curl_URL *u, char *hostname,
  * example is too big, this function returns HOST_NAME.
  *
  * Output the "normalized" version of that input string in plain quad decimal
  * integers.
  *
+ * A single dot following the numerical address is accepted and "swallowed" as
+ * if it was never there.
+ *
  * Returns the host type.
  *
  * @unittest 1675
  */
 
@@ -525,21 +528,30 @@ UNITTEST int ipv4_normalize(struct dynbuf *host)
         rc = curlx_str_octal(&c, &l, UINT_MAX);
     }
     else
       rc = curlx_str_number(&c, &l, UINT_MAX);
 
-    if(rc)
-      return HOST_NAME;
-
-    parts[n] = (unsigned int)l;
+    if(rc) {
+      if(!n || (rc != STRE_NO_NUM) || *c)
+        return HOST_NAME;
+      n--;
+    }
+    else
+      parts[n] = (unsigned int)l;
 
     switch(*c) {
     case '.':
-      if(n == 3)
-        return HOST_NAME;
-      n++;
-      c++;
+      if(n == 3) {
+        if(c[1])
+          /* something follows this dot */
+          return HOST_NAME;
+        done = TRUE;
+      }
+      else {
+        n++;
+        c++;
+      }
       break;
 
     case '\0':
       done = TRUE;
       break;

fix_commit.message: urlapi: prevent a terminal `.0x` component to normalize IPv4
fix_commit.author: Daniel Stenberg

findings.title: Terminal '.0x' component incorrectly normalized as valid IPv4
findings.message: ipv4_normalize() was changed to tolerate a failing numeric-parse (rc != 0) as a 'trailing dot was swallowed' case whenever the prior component index n is nonzero, the failure code is STRE_NO_NUM, and the cursor c now points at the string terminator. This check is applied uniformly after the '0'/'0x'/'0' (octal)/decimal number-parsing dispatch, but it does not distinguish between a genuine trailing-dot situation (e.g. '127.1.') and a component that began with the hex prefix '0x' but contained no hex digits after it (e.g. the final component in '127.1.0x'). In the latter case, curlx_str_hex() advances c past the consumed '0x' prefix, fails to find any digit, sets rc to STRE_NO_NUM, and leaves *c as '\0' (end of string) -- which makes the generic 'n && rc == STRE_NO_NUM && !*c' leniency check at line 534 treat the malformed '.0x' terminal component as if it were simply a legitimate trailing dot, decrementing n and accepting the host as a valid, fully-specified IPv4 address. This lets strings such as 'https://127.1.0x' normalize/parse as IPv4 host '127.0.0.1' even though '0x' is not a valid numeric component, which can confuse consumers that rely on urlapi's IPv4 host classification/normalization for security decisions (e.g. SSRF filtering, host allow/deny lists).
findings.suggestion: After the hex-specific parse (curlx_str_hex), immediately check its own rc and return HOST_NAME on failure before falling through to the generic/shared 'trailing dot' leniency check, since that generic check was designed only for the trailing-dot case and is not valid for a '0x' prefix with no following hex digits.

ground_truth.root_cause: Commit 831a1514843bfa4d4d006627 (urlapi: consume trailing dots after IPv4 numerical addresses) replaced the previous unconditional 'if(rc) return HOST_NAME;' check after the number-parsing dispatch with a conditional that allows a failed parse to be tolerated when n is nonzero, rc == STRE_NO_NUM, and the cursor is at the end of the string -- intending to permit a trailing dot after the last IPv4 octet to be silently dropped. However this same lenient path is also reachable when the component begins with the '0x' prefix (handled by curlx_str_hex) but contains no hex digits at all, because curlx_str_hex also returns STRE_NO_NUM and leaves the cursor at end-of-string in that scenario. The code did not special-case the hex-prefix branch to reject rc failures immediately, so a hex-prefixed-but-empty terminal component is misclassified as the 'trailing dot was swallowed' case.

must_cover.reason: Primary location of finding: Terminal '.0x' component incorrectly normalized as valid IPv4
